subject: biology-1
question: A single epinephrine molecule can ultimately cause a liver cell to release millions of glucose molecules from stored glycogen. Which property of **signal amplification** explains how one molecule produces such a large effect?

options.text: One receptor can bind many epinephrine molecules at the same time.
Epinephrine is hydrophobic and passes through the membrane, so it can activate many receptors.
At each step of the cascade, one activated molecule switches on many molecules of the next type, multiplying the message at every level.
The same epinephrine molecule is reused many times by the response machinery.

explanation: Amplification works because every cascade step activates multiple copies of the next component, so the effect multiplies geometrically from one receptor to many enzymes and finally to a flood of product molecules. A is backwards, because each receptor binds one ligand at a time. B misidentifies epinephrine, which is hydrophilic and acts at the surface, and D misstates the ligand's role, since epinephrine is not reused by the response machinery.
